title: Inventions and Ideas
objectives: I can explain ten words for judging and describing inventions and designs.
I can tell what makes a design convenient, sturdy, durable, or automatic.
I can use the endings -ment and -ion to understand words about making and using machines.
I can write a short design report that uses exact words and gives reasons.
rationale: Words for judging designs (durable, sturdy, convenient, automatic) connect science units to everyday decisions and prepare students for the evaluative language of argument. The ten words sort into things people make (device, gadget, blueprint), actions of makers (improve, operate, assemble), and qualities of a good design (convenient, durable, automatic, sturdy). Friction and propel return from unit 5 as design problems, and capable returns from unit 1. The passage is an invented story about a student inventor, so every detail of the build can be taught as plausible fiction.

words.def: A tool or machine made for one job.
words.ex: A thermometer is a device that measures how warm or cool something is.
words.ex2: The new device in our classroom counts how many people walk through the door.
words.nonExample: A rock found on the ground is not a device, because no one built it for a job.

apps.academic: In science class, a device such as a scale or a ruler helps you measure.
apps.spoken: My dad has a device that tells him how many steps he walks.
apps.writing: Use device for a made object that does one clear job.

cloze.s: The nurse used a small ___ to measure the girl's temperature in just a few seconds.

cloze2.s: A smoke alarm is a ___ that warns people about fire so they can get out safely.

misuse.s: A device is a natural thing that grows from a seed and needs sunlight.
misuse.why: A device is made by people for a job; a plant that grows from a seed is natural.

words.frame: A device that I use is ___.

words.ex: Daily reading will improve your vocabulary.
words.ex2: The engineers worked to improve the bridge after the first test.
words.nonExample: Making something worse is not improving it.

apps.academic: Engineers test a design, find a problem, and improve it.
apps.spoken: I want to improve my free throw.
apps.writing: Use improve for any change that makes something better.

cloze.s: Practicing every day helped Gabe ___ his swimming, and his times dropped each week.

cloze2.s: The cook added more spice to ___ the soup after the first taste.

misuse.s: He tried to improve his grade by skipping every test, so his score dropped.

words.def: To work or to make a machine work.
words.ex: The pilot knows how to operate the controls of the helicopter.
words.ex2: This little robot can operate on batteries for ten hours.
words.nonExample: A broken toaster sitting on the shelf does not operate.

apps.academic: Instructions explain how to operate a machine safely.
apps.spoken: I can operate this camera by myself.
apps.writing: Use operate for working a machine or for a machine that is working.

cloze.s: Only adults with a license may ___ the heavy crane at the building site.

cloze2.s: Solar panels allow the small lamp to ___ without a battery.

misuse.s: The machine would operate perfectly even when it was unplugged and broken.
misuse.why: A machine that is unplugged and broken cannot operate.

words.def: Easy to use or close by when you need it.
words.ex: A bus stop right outside the school is convenient for students.
words.ex2: It is convenient to keep a spare pencil in your backpack pocket.
words.nonExample: A store a long drive away is not convenient for a quick snack.

apps.academic: A good design is convenient when it saves time or steps.
apps.spoken: That's convenient; the bus stops right here.
apps.writing: Use convenient to tell why something is easy or close.

cloze.s: The grocery store is ___ because it is only one block from our front door.

cloze2.s: A lunch box with a built-in ice pack is ___ on hot days when you cannot reach a refrigerator.

misuse.s: The bus stop was convenient because we had to walk five miles to reach it.
misuse.why: Convenient means easy and close; a five-mile walk is neither.

words.def: A small tool or machine that does a clever job.
words.ex: Her favorite kitchen gadget peels an apple in seconds.
words.ex2: My uncle collects gadgets, such as a flashlight that also charges his phone.
words.nonExample: A huge bulldozer is not a gadget, because gadgets are small.

apps.academic: An inventor may make a gadget to solve a small, daily problem.
apps.spoken: I got a new gadget for my birthday.
apps.writing: Use gadget for a small, clever tool or machine.

cloze.s: He pulled a tiny ___ from his pocket that peeled, cut, and opened cans all in one.

cloze2.s: The kitchen ___ chops an onion in two seconds, so nobody has to cry.

misuse.s: A gadget is a giant machine as big as a house.
misuse.why: A gadget is small; a machine as big as a house is not.

visual.alt: A small wrench next to a light bulb.

words.def: A detailed drawing that shows how to build something.
words.ex: The builders studied the blueprint before they laid the first brick.
words.ex2: Before building the model bridge, the class drew a blueprint on graph paper.
words.nonExample: A photograph of a finished house is not a blueprint, because it does not show how to build it.

apps.academic: A blueprint shows measurements so builders can follow the plan exactly.
apps.spoken: We drew a blueprint of our clubhouse.
apps.writing: Use blueprint for a drawing with sizes and parts that guides a builder.

cloze.s: The architect unrolled the ___ and pointed to where each wall and window would go.

cloze2.s: Before cutting any wood, the club drew a ___ with every measurement marked.

misuse.s: The builders threw away the blueprint so they could follow its directions.
misuse.why: You cannot follow a blueprint after you throw it away.

words.def: Strong enough to last a long time without breaking.
words.ex: Durable boots can last through many muddy hikes.
words.ex2: The museum chose a durable floor that could handle thousands of visitors.
words.nonExample: A paper cup that falls apart in minutes is not durable.

apps.academic: Engineers choose durable materials for bridges so they last for many years.
apps.spoken: These shoes are durable; I've worn them for two years.
apps.writing: Use durable to praise something built to last.

cloze.s: Because the backpack is ___, it has survived four school years of being tossed on the floor.

cloze2.s: Playground builders pick ___ metal and thick plastic so the equipment lasts for decades.

misuse.s: The durable toy broke apart after one minute of play.
misuse.why: Durable means lasting a long time; breaking in one minute is the opposite.

visual.alt: A hiking boot next to an hourglass.

words.def: Working by itself without a person controlling it.
words.ex: The automatic doors opened as we walked toward the store.
words.ex2: An automatic sprinkler turns on every morning at six.
words.nonExample: A door you must pull open by hand is not automatic.

apps.academic: An automatic machine does its job without a person pressing a button each time.
apps.spoken: The light is automatic; it turns on when I walk in.
apps.writing: Use automatic for something that works on its own.

cloze.s: The ___ sprinklers switched on at dawn, so nobody had to touch a faucet.

cloze2.s: Our new dishwasher is ___: you press one button and it fills, washes, and drains by itself.

misuse.s: The automatic door stayed shut until a person pushed it open by hand.
misuse.why: Automatic means it works by itself; this door needed a person.

visual.alt: A sliding door opening with sparkles beside it.

words.def: To put parts together to make something.
words.ex: We will assemble the bookshelf from twelve wooden pieces and a bag of screws.
words.ex2: Each worker on the line must assemble one part of the toy car.
words.nonExample: Taking a toy apart is not assembling it.

apps.academic: Instructions often say how to assemble a model step by step.
apps.spoken: Can you help me assemble this chair?
apps.writing: Use assemble for putting separate parts together.

cloze.s: Dad needed an hour to ___ the new bed after he laid out all the parts on the floor.

cloze2.s: Workers on the line ___ one toy car every minute.

misuse.s: She assembled the puzzle by tearing every piece into smaller bits.
misuse.why: To assemble is to put parts together; tearing pieces apart is the opposite.

words.def: Strongly built and not easy to break or knock over.
words.ex: The sturdy ladder stayed still even when two people climbed it.
words.ex2: A sturdy fence kept the horses safely inside the field.
words.nonExample: A wobbly stack of cards is not sturdy.

apps.academic: A sturdy base keeps a tall model from tipping over.
apps.spoken: This table is sturdy; it doesn't wobble.
apps.writing: Use sturdy for something that holds up under weight or pushing.

cloze.s: Because the table was ___, it did not wobble when the kids stood on it.

cloze2.s: The old bridge was ___ enough to hold a loaded truck.

misuse.s: The sturdy chair collapsed the moment she touched it.
misuse.why: Sturdy means strong; a chair that collapses at a touch is not strong.

passage.title: Jamal's Drip Bottle
paras: Jamal's grandmother loved her tomato plants, but she often forgot to water them on busy days. Jamal wanted to help, so he planned a new gadget: a bottle that would slowly drip water into the soil all day. He drew a blueprint on graph paper that showed every part and its size.

Next he gathered materials. He needed a sturdy plastic bottle, a thin tube, and strong tape. A cardboard box would not be durable enough to stay outside in the rain, so Jamal chose materials that could last all summer.

He began to assemble the pieces on the porch. First he poked a tiny hole in the bottle cap. Then he turned the bottle upside down and pushed it into the soil. "This will be more convenient than carrying a watering can every day," he said.

The first test did not work. The hole was too big, and the water drained in an hour. Jamal decided to improve the design by making a smaller hole. This time the water dripped slowly, and the soil stayed damp. The device could operate all day without his help, so it was automatic. Soon every neighbor wanted one.

qs.q: In paragraph 2, the word "durable" most nearly means
choices: able to last a long time
qs.why: A durable material stays strong outside for the whole summer.

qs.q: Why does Jamal choose a plastic bottle instead of a cardboard box?
choices: Plastic is durable enough to stay outside in the rain.
A plastic bottle is bigger than a box.
qs.why: The text says a cardboard box would not be durable enough for rain.

qs.q: Why does Jamal make a smaller hole the second time?
choices: He wanted the bottle to look different.
The first hole let the water drain too fast.
qs.why: The water drained in an hour with the big hole, so a smaller hole slows the drip.

qs.q: Which detail best shows that the device is automatic?
choices: He drew a blueprint on graph paper.
He tested it on the porch.
It could operate all day without his help.
qs.why: Working all day without Jamal means the device works by itself.

qs.q: Which sentence tells the main idea of the passage?
choices: Gardens need to be watered every hour.
A student improved his invention by planning, testing, and making changes.
qs.why: Jamal plans, builds, tests, finds a problem, and improves the design.

teacher.overview: Students learn ten design words, read a story about a student inventor, practice the suffixes -ment and -ion, and write about how to judge and improve a design.

notes.va.device.n: Device is a general word for a made tool. Have students sort pictures into devices and natural objects.
notes.va.improve.v: Improve means make better, not just change. Ask what the change fixed.
notes.va.operate.v: Teach the sense of working a machine. Mention that doctors operate on patients, a different meaning to teach later.
notes.va.convenient.adj: Convenient is about ease and closeness. Students often confuse it with convenience store; show how the word describes anything easy.
notes.va.gadget.n: A gadget is small and clever. Students enjoy drawing their own; keep the focus on the job it does.
notes.va.blueprint.n: Blueprint is a compound of blue and print, but the meaning is not the sum. Use a real plan with measurements.
notes.va.durable.adj: Durable is about lasting over time; sturdy is about strength at one moment. Test both with a classroom object.
notes.va.automatic.adj: Automatic means it works by itself. Ask which classroom objects are automatic and which are manual.
notes.va.assemble.v: Use a small kit or building blocks. Compare assemble and dismantle.
notes.va.sturdy.adj: Sturdy is about being hard to knock over or break. Link to friction by asking how a wagon wheel stays steady.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'Jamal wants the bottle to last all summer outside. The text says a cardboard box would not be durable enough. Durable means strong enough to last, so plastic is a better choice. I can use durable in my own sentence: These boots are durable.'

How does a blueprint help an inventor avoid mistakes?
misconceptions: Durable and sturdy mean exactly the same thing.
extend: Design a gadget and label a blueprint with five unit words.
Test two materials, such as paper and plastic, for durability and write a short report.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit durable, sturdy, and automatic as quality words two days later, again at one week, and reuse friction, propel, and capable when students explain how a design works.

wida.oral: Partner A describes an object without naming it. Partner B guesses the object and tells whether it is durable, sturdy, convenient, or automatic.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (manejar for operate, aparato for gadget, robusto for sturdy, plano for blueprint) not reviewed by a native speaker; operate has several Spanish choices depending on context.
Operate is taught in the machine sense only; the medical sense is left for a later grade.
The passage is invented fiction; the slow-drip bottle is a plausible home project but was not tested.
